selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Where did the traveler go after leaving the gathering of the prophets?
questions.answer: He went to the classroom of truthful scholars.

questions.question: What was the job of these scholars in the passage?
questions.answer: Their job was to prove the truths of faith.

questions.question: Why is their agreement important?
questions.answer: Because many wise people agreed on the same faith truths.

questions.question: Why is their agreement even more meaningful?
questions.answer: Because they were not all the same in thinking and ability.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the example about closing one’s eyes in daytime?
questions.answer: A person cannot change the truth, only hide it from himself.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person can do only for himself by shutting his eyes?
questions.answer: He can make it seem dark only to himself.

questions.question: What had the scholars’ light done over many years?
questions.answer: It had lit up much of the world.

questions.question: Could the people who deny faith break that power?
questions.answer: No. Their combined strength could not shake it.

questions.question: Who invited the traveler into a new classroom?
questions.answer: Purified and very truthful scholars invited him.

questions.question: What made these scholars trustworthy in the passage?
questions.answer: They were very truthful and used powerful proofs.

questions.question: What did the traveler see in their classroom?
questions.answer: He saw many brilliant and honored scholars.

questions.question: What was special about their proofs?
questions.answer: Their proofs were so strong that they left no doubt.

questions.question: Did their different backgrounds stop them from agreeing?
questions.answer: No. They still agreed on the faith.

questions.question: What is surprising about the scholars’ agreement?
questions.answer: They agreed even though they had different ways of thinking.

questions.question: How does the passage describe someone who rejects these clear proofs?
questions.answer: As ignorant and stubborn.

questions.question: How far had that light spread?
questions.answer: It had spread across half the world.

questions.question: For how long had the classroom’s light been shining?
questions.answer: For more than a thousand years.

questions.question: What short statement sums up the scholars’ lesson?
questions.answer: Their united and certain proofs point to Allah alone.

questions.question: What kind of place did he enter in this part?
questions.answer: He entered a classroom of purified scholars.

questions.question: What does it show when many scholars agree on the same pillars of belief?
questions.answer: It shows the beliefs rest on strong truth.

questions.question: What kind of strength did the traveler find in that classroom?
questions.answer: He found strong moral and spiritual power.

questions.question: After the prophets, what group taught the traveler next?
questions.answer: A group of purified scholars taught him.

questions.question: How long had the scholars’ light continued?
questions.answer: It had continued for over a thousand years.

questions.question: Who were the teachers in this passage?
questions.answer: The teachers were purified and truthful scholars.
